history.dynasty: No documented builder; the Parmar dynasty claims Arbuda Devi as its ancestral goddess - Parmar rulers are believed to have originated at Mount Abu from the Agnikund (fire pit) (verify - from travel sources).
history.period: Antiquity claims ('thousands of years old', '5000 years old', Shakti Peetha) are unverified
history.summary: Adhar Devi, also called Arbuda Devi, is a Hindu rock-cut cave temple dedicated to a form of Goddess Durga (Katyayani), about 3 km north of Mount Abu. Legend holds that the goddess's 'Adhar' (support/lip) fell here and hung in mid-air, giving the temple its name; it is claimed as a Shakti Peetha (verify). The shrine is cut out of one huge solid piece of rock and reached by crawling through a narrow cave opening; it is often cited as one of the finest rock-cut temples of the region. Reaching it requires a steep climb - sources variously say 365 steps (lightuptemples, Holidify) or 400-500 steps (Tripadvisor reviews); the climb, through wooded slopes with a sheer rock face used by climbers, takes about 45 minutes and is not recommended for the elderly. Near the temple is Dhoodh Baori, a sacred well with milky-coloured water believed to manifest the celestial cow Kamadhenu, which also serves as the temple's water source. Navratri is the grandest festival here. Photography and mobiles are prohibited inside. FLAG: duplicate of CSV row 2179 'Adhar Devi Mandir (Arbuda Mata Mandir)' - same temple; dedup needed. Coordinates are geocoded and approximate.

name: Adhar Devi Temple (Arbuda Devi)
town_description: Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, in the Aravalli range of Sirohi district at about 1,219 m, built around the Nakki Lake. The Adhar/Arbuda Devi cave temple lies about 2-3 km north of the town, on a wooded hillside above the main road; from its height visitors get a wide view over the town. It is one of Mount Abu's most important Hindu pilgrimage points, alongside the Dilwara Jain temples and the Achaleshwar Shiva temple.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport, Dabok/Udaipur, about 175 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Abu Road station, about 28 km away (verify); taxis and buses connect to Mount Abu.
travel.road: About 2-3 km north of Mount Abu town / bus stand, reachable by local taxi; from the road a steep climb of ~365-500 steps (verify the count) leads to the cave shrine. Wear comfortable footwear; the climb is not recommended for aged visitors.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (September-October) is the grandest and most crowded period. Avoid the midday heat for the climb.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 5:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM - 8:00 PM daily (per Holidify - verify). No entry fee. Time required: 1-2 hours including the climb.
